name: How does Level 5 drywall finishing differ from Level 4?
description: Level 5 includes a full skim coat over the entire drywall surface, unlike Level 4 which only applies compound to joints and fasteners.

mainEntity.name: How does Level 5 drywall finishing differ from Level 4?

acceptedAnswer.text: The primary difference between Level 4 and Level 5 drywall finishing lies in the extent of the joint compound application. Level 4 involves taping and three coats of joint compound over joints and fasteners, feathering out the edges. While it provides a good, smooth surface, it doesn't cover the entire wall. Level 5, conversely, applies a thin skim coat of joint compound over the *entire* drywall surface after Level 4 is complete. This full skim coat eliminates any texture variations between the paper and the mudded areas, ensuring a perfectly uniform porosity and smoothness, critical for demanding finishes.
